# Autolyse

Mixing only the flour and water, then leaving the dough to rest for 20 to 60 minutes before adding the levain and salt. During the rest the flour hydrates fully and gluten starts to form on its own, so the dough needs less mixing afterwards.

## How we use it

Kofi uses a 30-minute autolyse on the house sourdough and the seeded rye, mixed at 04:35 so the rest overlaps with the first bake going in. On the white sourdough it shortens the mixer time by about three minutes and gives a more open crumb. He does not use it on the baguette dough.

## Caveat

With the stone-ground Tarnwick flour the autolyse needs to be shorter in warm weather, or the dough goes slack before the salt goes in. Kofi adjusts by feel; it is not written down anywhere yet.
